lesson.menu_title: Living With the Kanes — House Rules Without a Fight
lesson.menu_desc: Curfew, chores and asking for things politely -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- Living With the Kanes: House Rules Without a Fight
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Laís Paludetto Rodrigues | Lesson 3 -- Living With the Kanes

listenings.text: Okay, so, house tour, part two. Nothing here is complicated, I promise. Breakfast is whenever you want, but if you take the last of the milk, you have to write it on the board by the fridge. That board is the only rule I really care about. You don't have to eat dinner with us every night, but we do eat together around seven, and Emma will complain loudly if you skip it. On school nights we ask everybody to be home by ten, and on Fridays and Saturdays it's midnight. If you're going to be late, you don't need permission, you just need to text. And you can use the washing machine any time except after nine at night, because the wall is thin and my wife sleeps early.

Hi Lais, it's Maya, Greg's wife. I'm at work until six today, so I'll leave a note for you here. You don't have to cook anything tonight, there are leftovers from yesterday in the blue container. Please take them out of the fridge around half past six so they are not freezing. Two small things. You are allowed to invite friends over, of course, but let one of us know in the morning, not when they are already at the door. And could you put your laundry basket outside your room on Sundays? I do a big wash on Sunday evenings and it is easier if everything is in one place. That's it. See you at dinner.

extra_audio.text: Greg shows Lais the board by the fridge and explains the milk rule. He tells her that the family eats dinner together at around seven. Lais asks what time she has to be home on school nights. Greg says ten on school nights and midnight at the weekend. Lais asks whether she is allowed to invite a friend over on Saturday.

items.situation: You want to invite two friends over on Saturday afternoon. Ask your host mum, and give her the details before she asks for them.
tips: Would it be okay if I invited two friends on Saturday?
They'd come around three and leave before dinner.
Is there anything I should do first?

items.situation: A school event finishes at half past ten on a Wednesday, and curfew is ten. Explain the situation and ask.
tips: The school play finishes at half past ten.
Would you mind if I got home a bit later, just this once?
I can text you when I leave.

items.situation: You have no idea how the washing machine works and you do not want to break it. Ask.
tips: Could you show me how the washing machine works?
I don't want to press the wrong button.
Which one do I use for dark clothes?

items.situation: Your host family eats dinner at seven and you have a video call with Brazil at exactly that time on Tuesdays. Bring it up.
tips: Can I bring something up about Tuesdays?
My family calls me at seven, because of the time difference.
Would it be a problem if I ate a bit later that day?

items.situation: You broke a glass in the kitchen. Say what happened and offer to fix it.
tips: I'm really sorry, I broke a glass this morning.
I'd like to replace it. Where did you buy them?

items.situation: You want to know which jobs around the house are yours. Ask so that nobody has to remind you later.
tips: Do I have to do anything on weekdays?
I'd rather know now than get it wrong.
